---
title: Baking sourdough bread at home
lang: en
free: true
---

Sourdough bread rises without commercial yeast. Instead it uses a starter — a living culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria kept alive by regular feeding with flour and water.

## Building the starter

Mix equal weights of flour and water and leave it at room temperature. Discard half and feed it fresh flour every day. After about a week it should double in size a few hours after feeding, smelling pleasantly sour. That tang comes from the bacteria producing lactic and acetic acid.

## Mixing and fermentation

Combine the active starter with flour, water and salt, then let the dough ferment slowly for several hours. During this bulk fermentation the gluten develops and the dough fills with gas. A series of gentle stretches and folds builds strength without kneading.

## Baking

Shape the loaf, let it proof, then bake in a very hot Dutch oven so steam is trapped around the crust. The result is an open crumb, a crackling crust, and a deep flavour that a quick yeasted loaf can never match.
